rivals.statement: Reachable tail with scattered errors: on most problems its 4 stored samples miss, the cued base still has a small right-answer probability (about 0.05-0.3 per sample), and its wrong answers there rarely repeat a value. So each extra independent sample adds coverage, and a right answer seen 2-3 times wins the plurality. Vote accuracy keeps following pass@k past k = 4 instead of stopping at pass@4 (467 on MATH-500).
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers took the 33 MATH-500 problems with no right answer in 4 samples as unreachable and the agreeing wrong groups at k = 4 as fixed, so they capped the vote near pass@4 minus those groups (about 454). Larger k both reaches the tail and breaks those coincidental groups.

holds_against.why: At k = 4, 9 of 21 vote failures had a wrong group of 2 or more. With scattered errors a 2-of-4 match is a coincidence, and 9 problems is less than half of the 18-problem rise from 449 to 466, so most such groups dissolve by k = 12.

A restart lifts the hard328 vote only 192 -> 195. It resamples only cap-hit draws, and those sit at the hard end of the difficulty axis (fact 4: RL does no better on them than on finished-wrong problems of matched difficulty). So it adds few tail draws. New full samples on all problems do.

forecasts.reason: Vote@4 192, pass@4 205, and 123 problems at 0/4 with a reachable tail. MATH-500 went +7.4 from 4 to 6; the hard set has about twice the share of problems at mid and low p, so +9 to +11.
M(2) vote@3 246 against single samples around 233. A 4th independent sample adds tail coverage, and scattered errors keep 2-2 ties rare: +3 to +8.
Single samples 234, 229, 237. Seed-to-seed spread is about ±5.
Seed 3,010,000 gave 245 at cap 32,768. Think-SFT at seed 3,000,000 ran 4 below its other seed, so shade that down slightly.
Vote@4 at cap 16k is 75. About 12 more right answers per sample from finishing at 32k, with scattered errors, turn into plurality wins at more than hard328's 0.27 conversion rate.
Mean at 16k is 60 with about 62 cap hits. About 20 % of the 16k cap hits finish right at 32k (hard328: 23 of 93), and fresh problems are harder.
Seed 3,100,000 gave 232. Per-seed tail draws are large at this level, so regress toward Think-SFT plus the 1.5x-3x lift (about 220-226).
232 at T 1.0. T 0.6 trims tail draws in both directions, so the net change is about zero for an SFT model that does not loop.
474 at T 1.0, cap 32,768; MATH-500 is near ceiling, so T 0.6 moves it at most a few problems.
Think-SFT with the cue scores 457-462 at 16k. M(2)'s lift of about +7 points on hard328 shrinks near the ceiling.

rivals.statement: Split votes on covered problems: vote@4 falls short of pass@4 mainly through 2-2 and 1-1-1-1 splits and cap-hit abstentions on problems the base already solves at moderate rate. More samples resolve these splits, so the vote climbs to pass@4 (about 467) and stops there. On problems with no right answer in 4 samples the base keeps a shared wrong attractor, so a rare right draw loses the plurality. The vote rises fast, then hits a hard ceiling set by coverage.
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers read the 446-450 at k = 4 as close to the vote's limit and so did not see how many covered problems were lost only to split votes. At k = 12 those splits resolve almost completely, which puts the vote at 466, one below pass@4.

holds_against.why: The RL-written-examples arm solves 5 of 33 base-0/4 problems in one sample, about the rate of a fresh base sample. A right draw is possible, but against a repeated wrong value (fact 26: cued wrong answers agree more than chance, +0.13) one right draw does not win the plurality, so coverage at 0/4 never becomes vote wins.
Code-RL is right on 27 % of the base-0/4 problems, but it has different weights. That shows the problems are solvable, not that base samples reach them often enough to outvote its attractor.

forecasts.reason: On hard328 the vote@4 to pass@4 gap is 13 (192 vs 205). The two new samples resolve about a third of the splits; the 123 problems at 0/4 add nothing.
With 4 votes, 2-2 splits come back (Think-SFT's vote@4 241 sits at the top of its vote@3 range of 231-241), so the gain over vote@3's 246 is between -3 and +1.
Single samples 234, 229, 237.
245 at seed 3,010,000. Think-SFT is 4 lower at seed 3,000,000 than at 3,010,000.
Vote 75 at 16k. On hard328, going to 32k turned +22 per sample into only +6 in the vote, because late answers fall on attractor problems; the same conversion of about +12 per sample gives +3 to +4.
Mean 60 at 16k plus about 20 % of about 62 cap hits finishing right at 32k.
232 at one seed. Low per-seed spread on covered problems means only mild regression.
232 at T 1.0. The released T 0.6 setting does not cause loops in Think-SFT.
474 at T 1.0, cap 32,768, near ceiling.
Think-SFT with the cue scores 457-462. The RL delta's lift is small near the ceiling.
